needsDecision.item: R-7 least-privilege upload principal is not in the range
needsDecision.detail: No IAM user/role granting s3:PutObject on adversarial-runs/* and dynamodb:PutItem with a LeadingKeys condition appears in stacks/ or in the diff. If it is meant to be configured manually, R-7 should say so; note that any LeadingKeys condition written as the spec says (`ADV#test`, `ADV#code`) would deny the items the script actually writes (`ADV#ADVERSARIAL_TEST`).

needsDecision.item: E-46 vs R-120 when Bedrock denies the synthesiser
needsDecision.detail: packages/functest/src/generate.ts:137-139 (a line that predates this range: aa82ba8~1 line 123) turns every LLM throw, including AccessDenied, into a per-requirement skip, so a job with Bedrock access denied is persisted as `succeeded` with cached plans and N skips whose reason carries the raw SDK message. E-46 says the job is `failed`, the error redacted, and no partial artifacts are produced. One of the two rules has to give; this range made the skip list more visible (manifest.skipped, job.skips, review stage) without resolving it.

needsDecision.item: `.adversarial-review/` is tracked (commit fea19df) while the shared spec §4 still calls it git-ignored
needsDecision.detail: Tracked run folders put earlier reviews' `expected-behaviours.md` and `review.md` about the same code within reach of later blind passes (which have Read/Grep). If tracking is the intended policy, the spec and the blind-agent read rules need an explicit exclusion; if not, .gitignore needs the entry back.

needsDecision.item: changed_files handed to both passes omits files that are in `git diff --name-only aa82ba8~1...HEAD`
needsDecision.detail: packages/adversary/tests/{attacks,calibration.answer-key,calibration.fixtures,core,critic,critic-cache-shape,mutation,post-review,post-review-2,review}.test.ts, packages/adversary/tests/calibration.ts, packages/adversary/tsconfig.json and several calibration fixtures (e.g. testgen/create-get-ready/catalog.json) are in the range but not in the list. Pass 1's X-101 premise that the adversary package has no test changes is therefore wrong; those tests exist and were read here.

needsDecision.item: Is a `matchesType: number` literal on a property declared `integer` a R-133a contradiction?
needsDecision.detail: packages/adversary/src/grounding.ts:109-111 reports it as Critical (and the plan is withheld), while R-117b and the emitter's typeMatches (packages/functest/src/emit.ts:132) accept an integer for `number`. If integer ⊂ number is the intended reading, grounding withholds valid plans.
